correctness.rationale: A centrally symmetric projected hull conv{±P_E e_i} has diameter twice its largest vertex norm, giving D=2sqrt(1-m²), m=min|U_i|. The event m>=t in each of eight octants is the spherical patch u_i>=t; its Gauss–Bonnet area is 3α(t)-pi-3tβ(t), with α=arccos(t²/(1-t²)), β=pi/2-2arcsin(t/sqrt(1-t²)). Eight patches give Q(t)=2 area/pi and the stated complete CDF; differentiation α’=tβ’ yields exact positive density. At small t, f_m(t)=3-12t/pi+O(t³) gives the upper 3sqrt(eps)-6eps/pi tail. Near (1,1,1)/sqrt3, the rescaled spherical patch tends to the equilateral triangle sum(w)=0,w_i>=-1 with normalized area, giving lower coefficient 9sqrt3/(2pi), Dirichlet(1,1,1) and independent equally likely eight sign patterns. Symmetry gives uniform minimum-coordinate index and uniform scaled defect at the upper endpoint. Independently verified 2000 projected six-vertex configurations; analytic curvature and local-chart arguments prove the continuum law.

value.rationale: The projected diameter is an intrinsic and easily interpreted size observable of a classical regular polytope. Its full elementary law, sharp two-endpoint asymptotics, and conditional Dirichlet tangent geometry distinguish geometry at body-diagonal normals from coordinate-plane normals. These provide a natural exact reference distribution and a meaningful endpoint shape classification not implied by first moments or by a differently defined inradius.

final_claim: For the regular unit coordinate octahedron, the random Haar planar-shadow diameter is D=2sqrt(1-min_i|U_i|²); its complete elementary spherical-patch CDF and density, sharp lower/upper endpoint expansions, and conditional lower Dirichlet(1,1,1) orientation / upper uniform minimum-coordinate defect laws are determined.
